ONE CONFOUND NO GATE HERE REMOVES. The subject and the control differ in OCCUPANCY as well as in tile: at the production pin of num_stages=4 the resident-block ratio is 2:1, at 2 stages it is still 2:1, at 3 it is 3:1, and the only matched setting is 5 stages, which sm_80 cannot run and which unpins the comparison from every published arm. So no --num-stages choice disambiguates a result here, in either direction: a gap can be residency rather than tile, and an absent gap can be residency cancelling a tile effect. scripts/occupancy_vs_swizzle.py measures the residency effect directly, and its size is what to subtract before this verdict is read as being about the tile at all.

gates.name: V3 clocks
gates.prediction: every cell was timed at one clock, and every retained point is scored against the roof at the clock it ran
gates.rule: <= 10% of clocked cells drifting past 5% or LEVEL-low (under 95% of the roof's clock); LEVEL-high cells (over 105%) are kept and scored against the roof at their own clock

gates.invalidates: the fractions, in the direction stated below. Individual sagging cells are already excluded; a box that sags this often is not something an exclusion can fix
lines: 39 of 39 cells carry an under-load clock; session median of those 1590 MHz

4 cells drifted past 5% between their first and last under-load sample; 15 ran LOW, under 95% of the roof's clock; 21 ran HIGH, over 105% of it, and are KEPT; 4 points lost every repeat and are excluded

this session's median ran +7.1% against the 1485 MHz the roof was measured at. Direction: a LEVEL-high cell's fraction of the FIXED roof is OVERSTATED by its clock ratio, up to 1.20x here. Read `of roof at own clock`, which divides by roofline.roof_at_clock(roof, roof clock, cell clock); a memory-bound cell does not follow the SM clock, so that rescaled fraction is the comparable one and the fixed one is not.

points that lost EVERY repeat and left the gated set: [(128, 256), (128, 512), (128, 1024), (128, 2048)]. Losing the deepest one shortens the doubling chain, which C2 reports as a span too short rather than as a plateau.
